assumptions: The owner may set pilot prices and reserve limited service appointments.
context.composition_guidance: Combine a paid service offer with a bounded delivery arrangement; count all preparation and delivery effort.

constraints.text: Spend at most EUR 120 in total, with no recurring spending commitment.
Use at most six additional staff hours including preparation, contact and delivery, and finish within two weeks.
Use existing tools and the counter; no new software, hires or paid advertising.
Contact only the forty customers who opted in, using the existing email channel.

context.context_summary: One owner runs the shop. The goal is to test paid demand with existing tools and customer relationships, without committing to a continuing programme.

criteria.text: Itemise cash and staff time and show that the complete pilot fits both limits.
State the paid demand signal, assumptions and an observable continue-or-stop decision.
Offer materially different ways to test additional revenue, not changes of wording.

facts: The shop has ordinary bicycle repair tools and a service counter.
Forty existing customers have opted in to service emails.
The owner can devote six additional staff hours over the next two weeks.
The total additional cash allowance is EUR 120.
unknowns: Customer willingness to pay and response rate have not been measured.

request.request: Propose three distinct two-week pilots through which a neighbourhood bicycle repair shop could earn additional service revenue from existing customers, within the stated cash and staff-time limits.

assumptions: Customers with matching needs can be identified from replies within the opted-in list.
The owner sets a price and appointment cap that fit six total staff hours.
Any written-material or consumable cost stays within the EUR 120 one-off allowance.
Customers accept prepayment and attend their reserved appointments.

components.dimension: The paid service customers are invited to buy.
components.variant: A fixed-price safety and maintenance check covering inspection, adjustments and a short written recommendation.

components.dimension: How the shop limits and fulfils the service during the two-week pilot.
components.variant: Offer a small number of pre-booked counter appointments at set times.

components.dimension: Which opted-in existing customers receive the offer or priority access.
components.variant: Email all forty customers a short choice of service needs and allocate the limited offer to replies that match the pilot.

components.dimension: What customer agreement confirms demand before the owner spends time delivering the service.
components.variant: Require payment when the customer books a reserved place.

components.dimension: The explicit limit that keeps the experiment bounded while making its result observable.
components.variant: Set a maximum number of paid places and stop accepting bookings when they are filled.

proposals.proposal: Sell a fixed-price seasonal safety and maintenance check with inspection, adjustments and a short written recommendation, using pre-booked counter appointments for customers from the forty-person opted-in list who reply with a matching need, requiring prepayment and stopping at a hard capacity cap.
proposals.reason: The check is clearly defined, prepayment confirms demand before delivery, and the appointment and capacity limits can make the pilot bounded. Existing tools, the counter and the opted-in email list satisfy the resource and contact constraints. The proposal does not itemise price, materials, number or duration of appointments, email and follow-up effort, so it does not establish that the complete pilot fits EUR 120 and six hours; those limits require explicit conservative caps. The service is plausibly relevant but willingness to pay and response rate are unverified. It is materially different from the repair-bundle candidates in the kind of value sold, though the same general booking mechanism is used.

assumptions: The fixed price and number of slots are set so labour plus preparation, email, booking, payment handling and follow-up stay within six hours.
Any repair parts and consumables remain within the EUR 120 allowance.
Customers accurately identify a need matching the bundle and accept prepaid booking.

proposals.proposal: Offer a fixed-price minor-repair and tune-up bundle to opted-in customers who identify a matching need, using prepaid appointments capped at a small number of counter slots.
proposals.reason: The proposal uses only the existing email list, counter and tools, and prepayment confirms demand before delivery. A capacity cap can keep service within six hours and two weeks, and one-off materials can fit within EUR 120, but the candidate supplies no prices, slot count, service duration or materials budget, so complete feasibility is unproven. The observable signal is prepaid bookings; continue only if the cap fills or produces sufficient revenue, otherwise stop. It is materially distinct through selling a repair outcome and requiring payment upfront.

assumptions: The recent-interaction records identify a relevant need without contacting non-opted-in customers.
The owner can process the capped number of bicycles within six additional hours.
Prepayment can be handled with existing tools and no recurring cost.
Materials and consumables stay within EUR 120.
Customers accept the stated price and drop-off and collection windows.

components.dimension: The paid service customers are invited to buy.
components.variant: A fixed-price bundle combining a common minor repair with a defined tune-up or adjustment.

components.dimension: How the shop limits and fulfils the service during the two-week pilot.
components.variant: Accept bicycles during one or two defined drop-off windows and complete the service by a stated collection time.

components.dimension: Which opted-in existing customers receive the offer or priority access.
components.variant: Prioritise customers whose recent shop interaction suggests a relevant maintenance need, while staying within the opted-in list.

components.dimension: What customer agreement confirms demand before the owner spends time delivering the service.
components.variant: Require payment when the customer books a reserved place.

components.dimension: The explicit limit that keeps the experiment bounded while making its result observable.
components.variant: Run the offer until a stated additional-revenue target or the two-week deadline is reached.

proposals.proposal: Sell a fixed-price minor-repair and tune-up bundle during one or two defined drop-off windows, prioritising opted-in customers with a relevant recent shop interaction, requiring prepayment, and stopping at a stated revenue target or the two-week deadline.
proposals.reason: Prepayment provides a clear paid demand signal before delivery, and targeted selection plausibly improves relevance while remaining within the forty opted-in customers. Drop-off windows can reduce handling overhead and the revenue cap supplies an observable stop condition. The proposal still omits the revenue target, price, number of bicycles, service durations, preparation, collection and follow-up time, and cash itemisation, so the six-hour and EUR 120 limits are not proven without a tightly chosen cap. Prioritisation also assumes the shop has a compliant way to identify relevant recent interactions. Like candidate 5a003, it tests a repair bundle rather than a materially different service value.
